identity: A talking-head bookend opens and closes, but the body is a DECK: full-frame art-directed slides in a strict alternating pattern (item card -> concept card), one beat each, synced to the narration. The corpus exemplar teaches 'brands sell feelings': logo slide (Tesla on red fabric) -> script-font concept slide ('Innovation,') -> subversion slide ('not cars.'). Highest slide rate in the corpus (7.3 cards/10s) with every slide readable in under a second.

brand-slides.notes: Tesla/Coca-Cola/Rolex/Apple sequence; script serif for feelings, giant condensed sans for negations; b/w portrait-grid wall for 'people'; night-desk b-roll bridge; handle outro

rules.pattern: a repeating 2-3 slide unit per item: [icon/logo slide] -> [concept word in expressive type] -> [optional subversion slide]; the unit repeats for 3-5 items
rules.slide_design: each slide is ONE idea: a logo on a textured field, or 1-3 words centered; backgrounds alternate color fields (brand color, gradient, black, white)
rules.type_contrast: script/serif for the emotional concept, heavy condensed sans for the blunt correction — the contrast IS the joke/insight
rules.timing: each slide enters with the idea it explains and holds long enough for its information load; simple symbols can flash quickly while a comparison or unfamiliar label must breathe
rules.bookends: talking head opens with the promise and returns for 'the lesson is simple' + CTA
rules.grade: slides are flat graphic color; footage bookends stay muted

capability_notes: Closest family to current tools: add_color_screen + add_title_card + add_text templates cover the slide vocabulary; logo slides need user-supplied or generated images (generate_image). The dependency is deck PLANNING from the transcript (find the items and their concept/correction pairs) and sub-second slide pacing.
